title: Pteridophytes
notes: Some of the basic features of pteridophytes are given below: 1.
Pterodophytes grow in cool and shady terrestrial habitat.
Adult plant body is sporophyte and truly differentiated into leaves, stem and roots.
They are vascular plant having presence of both xylem and phloem tissue.
Leaves may simple, minute and sessile or petiolate.
The primary root is short lived which is replaced by adventitious roots.
The stems are usually herbaceous and branched monopodially or dichotomously.
Reproduction is through spores which are formed in sporangia.
